title: Derived scalar extensions along a tower of fields compose
statement: For a field extension $K\subset L$ let $T_{L/K}:D(K)\to D(L)$ be the functor of derived categories of vector spaces [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] induced [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] by the exact functor $-\otimes_KL$ [lem-weil-field-scalar-extension-exact, def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension] applied termwise to complexes, with its canonical isomorphism $\alpha_{L/K}:T_{L/K}(Q C)\cong Q(C\otimes_KL)$ for complexes $C$ ($Q$ the localization functor). Then: (1) there is a unique natural isomorphism $\iota_K:T_{K/K}\cong\operatorname{id}_{D(K)}$ whose value at $QC$, composed with $\alpha_{K/K}^{-1}$, is $Q$ of the termwise isomorphism $C^r\otimes_KK\cong C^r$; (2) for a tower $K\subset L\subset M$ there is a unique natural isomorphism $c_{M/L/K}:T_{M/L}\circ T_{L/K}\cong T_{M/K}$ whose value at $QC$, conjugated by the isomorphisms $\alpha$, is $Q$ of the termwise tower isomorphism $(C^r\otimes_KL)\otimes_LM\cong C^r\otimes_KM$ of [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]; (3) these isomorphisms are coherent: $c_{L/L/K}$ and $c_{L/K/K}$ are induced by $\iota_L$ and $\iota_K$, and for $K\subset L\subset M\subset N$ the two isomorphisms $T_{N/M}T_{M/L}T_{L/K}\cong T_{N/K}$ built from the $c$'s agree. Moreover each $c_{M/L/K}$ and $\iota_K$ commutes with the shift isomorphisms of the triangulated functors.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal C_K=\mathrm{CoCh}(\operatorname{Mod}_K)$, $Q_K:\mathcal C_K\to D(K)$, and $E_{L/K}:\mathcal C_K\to\mathcal C_L$ for termwise scalar extension. By [lem-weil-field-scalar-extension-exact] the vector-space functor is additive and exact. Hence [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] supplies its termwise induced triangulated functor $T_{L/K}$, with the canonical factorization $\alpha_{L/K}:T_{L/K}Q_K\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_LE_{L/K}$ specified in the statement. The meaning of termwise induced is precisely this factorization. If $f:C\to C^{\prime}$ is a quasi-isomorphism, $Q_K(f)$ is invertible by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; naturality gives $Q_L(E_{L/K}f)=\alpha_{L/K,C^{\prime}}\circ T_{L/K}(Q_Kf)\circ\alpha_{L/K,C}^{-1}$, so this is invertible as well. Thus $Q_LE_{L/K}$ inverts the localization class, without requiring a separate tensor-cohomology theorem. Iterating this factorization shows that $Q$ after any composite of the $E$ functors also inverts quasi-isomorphisms. All categories use the universes fixed in the abstract-derived-category node.

source.place: Tag 015F, lemma-right-derived-exact-functor; Tag 05RU, definition-unbounded-derived-category. The natural factorization is the meaning of the functor induced from termwise scalar extension.

proof.text: Construct $u_C:E_{K/K}C\to C$ degreewise by $v\otimes a\mapsto av$, with inverse $v\mapsto v\otimes1$. The balancing relation gives $(av)\otimes1=v\otimes a$, so both composites are identities. A differential or a linear map commutes with multiplication by $a$; hence $u_C$ is an isomorphism of complexes natural in $C$. This uses the tensor product and its map-on-pure-tensors definition in [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], rather than an extra lemma about a derived identity functor.

source.place: Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product: balancing and the universal property of the tensor product; elementary identity specialization.

proof.text: For $K\subset L\subset M$, apply the natural tower isomorphism of [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension] in each degree. It gives $a_C:E_{M/L}E_{L/K}C\xrightarrow{\sim}E_{M/K}C$, $((v\otimes\lambda)\otimes\mu)\mapsto v\otimes(\lambda\mu)$. It commutes with the differential because both orders send this generator to $d_Cv\otimes\lambda\mu$, and it commutes with a chain map $f$ because both orders give $f(v)\otimes\lambda\mu$. Its inverse is $v\otimes\mu\mapsto(v\otimes1)\otimes\mu$, as follows from the $L$-balancing relation. Thus $a$ is a natural isomorphism on complex categories.

source.place: Tag 00CV, section-tensor-product; Tag 00D0, lemma-transitive, underlying tensor associativity. The tower isomorphism is already stated by the cited node.

proof.text: Apply part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to $Q_K$, with target $D(K)$, to the natural isomorphism $Q_Ku:Q_KE_{K/K}\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_K$ and the lifted functors $T_{K/K}$ and $\operatorname{id}$. Their factorization isomorphisms are $\alpha_{K/K}$ and the identity. This produces a natural isomorphism $\iota_K$ with $\iota_{K,Q_KC}=Q_K(u_C)\circ\alpha_{K/K,C}$. In particular $\iota_{K,Q_KC}\circ\alpha_{K/K,C}^{-1}=Q_K(u_C)$, exactly the required normalization. Part (2), or part (3) applied to two candidate hom transformations, proves uniqueness with that normalization.

proof.text: For a tower form the natural isomorphism $\beta_C=\alpha_{M/L,E_{L/K}C}\circ T_{M/L}(\alpha_{L/K,C}):T_{M/L}T_{L/K}Q_KC\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_ME_{M/L}E_{L/K}C$. Both complex-level functors $Q_ME_{M/L}E_{L/K}$ and $Q_ME_{M/K}$ invert quasi-isomorphisms, by step 1. Apply part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] with $Q_K$, target $D(M)$, their lifts $T_{M/L}T_{L/K},T_{M/K}$ and factorizations $\beta,\alpha_{M/K}$, to the natural isomorphism $Q_Ma$. The result is $c_{M/L/K}$, uniquely characterized by $c_{M/L/K,Q_KC}=\alpha_{M/K,C}^{-1}\circ Q_M(a_C)\circ\beta_C$. Descent of the inverse of $a$ proves invertibility. This displayed equation supplies the requested conjugation formula with every factor specified.

source.place: Tag 04VG, lemma-properties-left-localization, localization setting; part (2) of the cited universal-property node, using the natural tower map constructed in step 3.

proof.text: The two unit equations already hold on complexes. For $K\subset L$, $a_{L/L/K,C}=u_{E_{L/K}C}$ since both send $(v\otimes\lambda)\otimes\mu$ to $v\otimes\lambda\mu$. Also $a_{L/K/K,C}=E_{L/K}(u_C)$ since $(av)\otimes\mu=v\otimes a\mu$ for $a\in K$. These equalities follow directly from the tensor maps of [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. Substitute the formulas of steps 4 and 5. In the first equation naturality of $\iota_L$ for $\alpha_{L/K,C}$ identifies the resulting component with $\iota_{L,T_{L/K}Q_KC}$; in the second, naturality of $\alpha_{L/K}$ for $u_C$ identifies it with $T_{L/K}(\iota_{K,Q_KC})$. In both cases adjacent $\alpha\alpha^{-1}$ cancel. Part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] then gives $c_{L/L/K}=\iota_L T_{L/K}$ and $c_{L/K/K}=T_{L/K}\iota_K$ as natural transformations on $D(K)$, with the ordinary functor unit identifications.

u)$; associativity in $N$ makes them equal, and iterated tensor balancing and additivity extend the equality to every element in every degree [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. To pass to derived categories, precompose the proposed two composites of $c$ with $Q_K$. Use the formula of step 5 twice and naturality of each $\alpha$ with respect to the chain map $a$. Both composites then have the same source identification $\alpha_{N/M,E_{M/L}E_{L/K}C}\circ T_{N/M}(\alpha_{M/L,E_{L/K}C})\circ T_{N/M}T_{M/L}(\alpha_{L/K,C})$ and target identification $\alpha_{N/K,C}$; between them they are $Q_N$ of the two equal chain maps just calculated. Their components therefore agree at $Q_KC$. Part (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] proves equality everywhere, including the canonical functor reassociations.

proof.text: Finally check shifts, rather than inferring compatibility from the fact that the functors are triangulated. For every $n\in\mathbf Z$, termwise extension and shift have the canonical comparison $s_{L/K,n,C}:E_{L/K}(C[n])\xrightarrow{\sim}(E_{L/K}C)[n]$, whose degree-$r$ map is the identity on $C^{r+n}\otimes_KL$. Both differentials are $(-1)^n(d_C\otimes1)$, so this is a chain isomorphism. Reindexing the explicit formulas gives $u_{C[n]}=u_C[n]\circ s_{K/K,n,C}$ and $s_{M/K,n,C}\circ a_{C[n]}=a_C[n]\circ s_{M/L,n,E_{L/K}C}\circ E_{M/L}(s_{L/K,n,C})$. In the second equation both sides have source $E_{M/L}E_{L/K}(C[n])$ and target $(E_{M/K}C)[n]$; the comparison for the identity functor in the first equation is the identity. This is an equality on pure tensors in each degree [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension]. By [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $Q$ commutes with shifts. The canonical shift comparison of the induced functor of [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] is obtained by descending $s$ and these comparisons for $Q$; hence its defining equation makes $\alpha$ shift-compatible. Explicitly, if $q_{K,n,C}:Q_K(C[n])\to(Q_KC)[n]$ and $\gamma_{L/K,n,X}:T_{L/K}(X[n])\to(T_{L/K}X)[n]$, that equation is $\alpha_{L/K,C}[n]\circ\gamma_{L/K,n,Q_KC}\circ T_{L/K}(q_{K,n,C})=q_{L,n,E_{L/K}C}\circ Q_L(s_{L/K,n,C})\circ\alpha_{L/K,C[n]}$. Existence and uniqueness of this descended comparison follow from part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]; this spells out the canonical construction, not an additional assumption on $\alpha$. For $\theta=\iota_K$ or $c_{M/L/K}$, substitute the formulas of steps 4 and 5 into the desired equation $\gamma_{G,n,X}\circ\theta_{X[n]}=\theta_X[n]\circ\gamma_{F,n,X}$, where $F,G$ are its source and target functors and composite functors have their composite shift comparisons. At $X=Q_KC$, use the displayed defining equation and naturality of $\theta$ along $q_{K,n,C}$ to cancel the $\alpha$ and $q$ factors. What remains is $Q$ of the already verified equality for $u$ or $a$. Part (3) of the same localization node then proves the equation for every $X\in D(K)$. Thus both isomorphisms commute with every integer shift.
